lines.en: I started reading again.
Not words that I should or words that I’m meant to, but words that make the pain more painful and remind me why I limp when a girl with red hair would rather be the splint I never asked for.
A blueish glow bleeds out from the screen of my phone, but the vision it carries with it is not one with inflated breasts nor hair in private places, no.
It carries with it, words.
Words that make the pain more-
You already know.
I already told you.
This one is particularly relevant. And it goes like this.
It's late. I've come\nto find the flower which blossoms\nlike a saint dying upside down.
The rose won't do, nor the iris.\nI've come to find the moody one, the shy one,\ndowncast, grave, and isolated.
Now, blackness gathers in the grass,\nand I am on my hands and knees.\nWhat is its name?
Little sister, my indigo,\nmy secret, vaginal and sweet, you unfurl yourself shamelessly\ntoward the ground.
You burn. You live\na while in two worlds at once.
This one is called “My Indigo” and it makes me feel a little less alone.
But the way I’m feeling doesn’t matter now when there’s so much left unfelt.
Like cholera I spread, siphoning the moisture that I’ve come to know as complacency from everything and everyone — leaving a trail of excrement in my wake toward another resting place.
To properly spread, I must find water.
I hope I can remember how to swim.
: Hey.
: Long time, no see. How’s the bathhouse holding up?
: We’re closed for the night.
: Isn’t it a little early for-
: Sorry for the inconvenience.
I’ve spread a little faster than normal, I see.
I didn’t even need to enter the water.
: Is something wrong, Io?
: Something? No. Everything? Yes. But everything is always wrong because I’m basically just the human equivalent of a magnet that’s forgone its attraction to metal in place of tragedy.
: That sounds pretty rough. But hey, if it’s any consolation, I’ve felt more or less the same about myself lately.
: Mhm.
: That’s it? Not in the mood to talk tonight?
: Mhm.
: Are you mad at me or something?
: I should be.
: I should be a lot of things right now. But of course I can’t get a hold of my brain and tell it how to feel because, if I could do that, this wouldn’t be a problem in the first place.
: Trash will be trash, right? Is that a phrase? Because if it’s not, it is now. I’m making it a phrase.
: Then I’ve got one of my own in saying that one man’s trash is another man’s treasure.
: Hoarding is a trauma response. I’m not taking that as a compliment. Both because I don’t want to be complimented and because I think I am mad at you.
: For what?
: Something I don’t want to bring up because I don’t want you to be mad at me.
: That’s a little hypocritical, don’t you think?
: Have you been away for so long that you’ve already forgotten who you’re talking to right now?
: Depends. Have you forgotten how attached to me you’re supposed to be, even when we both know it’s wrong?
: I don’t think I ever said it was wrong.
: Well, you’re acting like it’s wrong.
: Can you just tell me why you’re here so I can come up with some sort of shitty excuse for why it’s a bad time?
: Can you look at me?
: I don’t know if that’s a good idea...It’ll make me want to talk to you.
: And if I talk to you, we’ll have to talk about the last few months. Which means we’ll mention things that have changed and things that we’ve learned.
: Then, that will naturally progress to you learning that I know a thing I’m not supposed to know and that you...
: That you may have...heard something about...someone who might...have stupid green hair or...is named Io...
: No one really talks about you, Io.
: Huh?
: It’s just hard to hear things about you when no one but Uta brings you up. And I’ve barely seen her lately either.
: So...you haven’t heard anything then? No rumors...or...anything at all?
: None whatsoever. So, about this thing that you’re not supposed to know-
: Sorry, I don’t have any idea what you’re talking about. And we’ve already spent too much of this reunion’s time on a thing I misunderstood. Quite thankfully at that.
: But-

: Nope! Besides, the thing I know is probably just another misunderstanding anyway. Or at least that’s what I’m going to tell myself so I can slink back into blissful ignorance, as forced as that bliss may be.

: But hey, bliss is a thing I’m already used to forcing. Mostly in the form of stuff that comes in translucent orange bottles. But you already know that since it’s the same stuff I almost killed Miku with.
: I was well aware of it long before she was even involved.
: Which she’s not anymore, by the way. She doesn’t need me now that she has a thing. Just like you don’t need me now that you have a thing.
: The only thing I have is an expired lease on life and the desire to lock myself in a padded room for the rest of eternity.
: Sounds like a better plan than wasting your breath on someone so worthless that her peers won’t even bring her up again after shining the spotlight on her for everyone to see.
: You should tell me what happened, Io.
: I’d rather fall asleep on an active tablesaw!
: Io-
: Just forget it, Sensei! Let’s seize this opportunity to go back to square one! Or...whatever square it was that we left off on before you went catatonic and I broke into your house.
: Yeah, about that. You might have noticed back when I met up with you and Miku at the park, but I’m not sure if I can just “go back.”
: And by “not sure,” I quite literally mean that I can not. So there’s a high likelihood that both of us are going to do nothing but shit all over ourselves in one another’s presence from now on.
: I think this might be the first time I’ve ever been excited to listen to someone whine before.
: For now, maybe. But there’s a good chance you’ll be the one who winds up getting sick of me at this rate.
: Wanna make a bet, then?
: Why not? If nothing else, it’ll give us one more paper-thin excuse to stay together.
: Then, I’ll bet you my life that you give up on me before I give up on you.
: And I’ll bet you mine that you’re wrong.
: So we both die either way.
: Poetic, isn’t it?
: A little cringey too, but that’s par for the course when it comes to people like us.
: But hey, this is a reunion! Which means that we should celebrate with greasy food and continued tales of why we hate the world that we were born in!
: Or fell in love with.
: Hm? Love? This place? I don’t get it.
: And I hope you never do.

Io and I head over to a fast food restaurant to medicate ourselves with food that would be called poison by most other standards. But, in a sense, poison is just as good as medicine for those who deserve death.

I’m talking about myself in regard to that last part, of course. Shocking, I know. But I don’t think that Io deserves death. Just maybe something along the same lines that Nodoka got after fucking with Yumi.
She isn’t feeling well, but I’m not sure if she’s always been this way or if it’s just more apparent to me now that I see this same faux-contentment every time I look in the mirror.

I wonder if it might have something to do with the fact that “something may have happened.” But I concede that whatever that wasn’t doesn’t have anything to do with me since I’m not her teacher anymore.
I have my life and she has hers. The rest of the girls have theirs too. And the best way for me to stay involved with them, since I can not tear myself away entirely, is to shed what matters least.
It’s okay to have things of your own. It’s okay to hide your problems from the people you don’t want to burden.
It’s okay to fake a smile while you’re doing that because maybe, just maybe, that smile will help someone.

So as the two of us, surrounded by smiles in a business that uses them as a marketing tactic, fake our happiness for the sake of one another, I take a bite out of a cheeseburger. But all I taste is flesh.
Flesh and the idea that I, too, have found myself in the mouth of a greater being.
But instead of trying to preserve myself, I just wonder how I must taste.
It must be good if so many chunks of me have been ripped out.
: So...hear any funny jokes lately?
: No. But I did go camping recently.
: Camping?! I want to go camping! Why didn’t you go with me?!
: Because I went with a bunch of older women and Ami instead.
: Ew. I didn’t like anything about that sentence.
: Yeah, that’s why I didn’t invite you.
I conveniently leave out the fact that she didn’t even cross my mind.
: You should go again, but with Uta and me next time. I’ve never gone before, but I’ve always wanted to try.
: Well, I’m glad at least you’re enthusiastic about it since Uta and I would very likely be useless.
: Uta wouldn’t be useless. She went camping all the time when she was little. She has a crossbow and everything.
: A crossbow? Exactly how long do you think we’d be camping for to warrant bringing that along?
: Hopefully for the rest of our lives. If the three of us start living off the grid, we can bypass taxes and grow our own food and stuff. It would be true freedom, Sensei.
: You’re in high school. You don’t pay taxes.
: I pay taxes when I buy things from the store, which is more than enough to make me know how much they suck and that we’d be better off without them.
: Fair enough. But even then, I can’t say I like the idea of living in the woods for the rest of my life.
: Yeah. It sounds nice in theory, but I wouldn’t be able to charge my power tools or watch baseball anymore, and those two things are basically half of the reasons I have to stay alive.
: Hey, that’s four more than I have.
: Think you’re broken enough to settle for someone like me yet, then? Maybe I could be your first reason if all this sudden trauma has lowered your standards by enough?
: Which isn’t to say they were high at all since you had no problem consenting to a relationship with that blonde who isn’t blonde anymore. Slight improvement, sure. But still gross.
: I’ll take blonde over green any day.
: Smart move. I hear that girls with green hair can be kind of psycho sometimes.
: Yeah, they never shut up either.
: They’re probably just so excited whenever someone acknowledges their worthless existence that they-
: Over here. There’s a table open this way.
: Huh?
: Can you believe that the ice cream machine is broken again? Has it ever worked?
: Mommy, can we go next door for dessert after dinner? Please?
: I don’t know, dear. I’m not sure if all of those calories are good for your health. It’s bad enough that we’re stopping at-
: Daaaaaaad? Pleeeeeeeease?
: Listen to your mother, sweetheart.
: But Mommy was going to get ice cream for herself! That’s not fair!
: That’s because Mommy is pregnant and if she doesn’t get what she wants, she’s going to kill all of us.
: Mommy will give you a bite of her ice cream when we get home, baby. Now, follow your father so we stop disturbing the other customers.
: Would you really kill me, Mommy?
: Robert, can you please tell your daughter I’m not actually a murderer?
: Not until I know for sure.
: Are you alright, Io?
: Yeah, I’m fine.
: Well, now I know you’re not fine. The Io Ichimonji I know would never miss out on an opportunity to self-deprecate, and I basically just handed you one on a silver platter.
: I just get annoyed when other people interrupt my conversations, that’s all.
: They weren’t really-
: I lost my train of thought. Now I can’t remember what I was talking about and I have to start all over. It’s annoying.
: And now they’re being loud...how am I supposed to focus?
: Io, they’re just eating. They’re not-
: Can we leave?
: I’m not feeling well all of a sudden.
Io had been tapping her knuckles on the table since we first showed up here.
She’s stopped now.
It’s like she’s focusing all she has on just maintaining composure and, as unfortunate as it is to say, I get it.

I don’t have to know why. And sure, I can guess to sate my own curiosity...But guessing will do nothing other than risk hurting her, and I’m not sure how much more pain that fragile frame of hers can take.
: Do you want me to ask if we can take this to go instead? Or-
: I’m not really hungry anymore. I just want to leave. Can we leave? Please?
: Please?
: Yeah.
: We can leave.
